result.summary:
Built a genuinely short-handed job by real clicking (job cmtumw4ry0011tvs43v4kw7vz "ZZTEST Client Alpha": Edit → Schedule & Team → Cleaners needed = 2, exactly one cleaner "ZZTEST Cleaner One" assigned, start moved to today 10:30 AM so the clock window was open) and drove it end to end as the cleaner, then repeated the admin half on a second short-handed job (cmtupslvr002rtvs4ogh6pc7a "ZZTEST Cap OK Client", released from hold).

The advisory contract holds where the controls exist. One wording — "Only 1 of 2 cleaners is on this job — 1 spot was never filled." — appeared verbatim on the my-jobs clock-in confirm, the /clock screen's inline block, the clock-out sheet, the admin Complete-job modal, and in the JobLog. Nothing was ever disabled and no server call refused: the cleaner clocked in (11:32 AM), clocked out (12:04 PM, 0h 32m) and the job closed COMPLETED, and the Logs tab carries "Finished short-staffed. Only 1 of 2 cleaners is on this job — 1 spot was never filled." beside the IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED row. A fully-staffed control job (required 1 / 2 assigned) opened no modal at all on Mark Complete, so the confirm really is conditional.

The crew-size union rule is correct at the predicate: this job's lead AND its only roster member are the same person, and every surface said "1 of 2" — a sum would have said 2 of 2 and shown nothing.

Two real problems. (1) The mark-arrived surface is unreachable: cleaners get the read-only CleanerCalendarClient drawer ("Read-only view — contact dispatch to make changes.", no buttons), and the CalendarJobActions employee branch that holds the "Mark arrived anyway" confirm is only mounted by the admin CalendarPageClient, which never sees role EMPLOYEE — so that quarter of the claim cannot be exercised by any user. (2) On the very screen that says "Only 1 of 2 cleaners", the cleaner's Team card says "Team 2 MEMBERS" and lists the same person twice (lead + roster), because it uses cleaners.length + (employee ? 1 : 0) — the exact sum the shared predicate exists to avoid.

Separately (not staffing-caused): "Complete anyway" reported success (header control flipped to "Get Review Link") but the job still reads Scheduled on fresh loads and in the jobs list; the fully-staffed control job behaved identically, so the staffing rule is not what stopped it.

Also worth knowing for the "both sides" wording: the admin has no clock-in/clock-out control at all (clockIn/clockOut are imported only by the cleaner components), so on the admin side Mark Complete is the only staffing-aware clock/complete control.
